sections.html:
Oklahoma City, the county seat, sits in this central Oklahoma county, which was formed in 1890 and covers 718 square miles. The 2020 population reached 796,292, among the biggest counts in the state. Edmond, Midwest City, Del City, Bethany and the other cities share the county's single assessor and single treasurer, even though each has different city and school levies on the bill.

Twelve cities and eight towns sit inside the lines. The cities are Bethany, Choctaw, Del City, Edmond, Harrah, Midwest City, Nichols Hills, Nicoma Park, Oklahoma City, Spencer, The Village and Warr Acres. The towns are Arcadia, Forest Park, Jones, Lake Aluma, Luther, Smith Village, Valley Brook and Woodlawn Park. Because Oklahoma City stretches over 620.79 square miles, a mailing address tells you little about which taxing units apply. The county property search shows the account for a specific parcel.

I-35, I-40 and I-44 cross the core, so buyers usually care about highway access. Hail and wind are the main roof concerns across the area, and a financed sale can slow if a roof carries hail damage or an old insurance claim, since lenders and appraisers ask about condition. A cash purchase as-is does not depend on a lender appraisal.

sections.h2: Who assesses a home and how to contest the value
sections.html:
Values are the job of the County Assessor, whose office is Suite 313 of the building at 320 Robert S. Kerr Avenue, Oklahoma City 73102. If you disagree, the route is a written protest to that same office. Notices of an increase tend to arrive in February, March or April, and each lists market value, taxable value (growth limited to 3 to 5 percent), the assessment percentage and the assessed value.

  • Step one: submit the Oklahoma Tax Commission protest form inside 30 days of the notice's mailing date.
  • Step two: take part in an informal hearing, by phone if you request it. Expect a written answer within 7 calendar days after that hearing.
  • Step three: if you disagree, go to the County Board of Equalization within 15 calendar days of the day the decision went out.
  • No change in value from the prior year? Your complaint is due by the first Monday in April.
  • A valuation you consider arbitrary has a shorter clock: 10 days from its notice.

The Board of Equalization meets from the fourth Monday in January until May 31.

Homestead status trims $1,000 from assessed value. In dollars, that is roughly $87 to $134 a year, depending on where the house sits. Eligibility means you owned the house and lived in it on January 1, with the deed signed by then and recorded with the County Clerk no later than February 1.

Households whose total income was $30,000 or less can claim a second $1,000. Heads of household who were 65 or older on January 1 and earn no more than the HUD median can request the senior valuation freeze, which locks the value at the taxable figure after that year's adjustments.

The application window opens January 1 and closes March 15, or 30 days after a valuation notice if that falls later. A new deed or a move means filing again. For a seller, that means your exemption stops when you sell, and your buyer starts from scratch.

Walk in, mail a check or go online. The Treasurer is in Suite 307 at 320 Robert S. Kerr, Oklahoma City 73102, though about 95 percent of what the county collects comes in by mail through an automated system.

Payment can be one lump or two halves. Lump sum or first half is due by December 31, and the second half by March 31. After December 31 an unpaid bill is delinquent from January 1. Interest is 18 percent a year, added as 1.5 percent each month on the 15th. A yearly tax resale auction is how the county deals with parcels that stay unpaid.

Bought a house lately? Tell the Assessor your mailing address before September 30. Accounts move to the Treasurer on October 1, and the statement goes to whatever address is on file.

A tax balance on the parcel is something the closing agent deals with, typically by subtracting it from what you receive. Ask the title company what amount it plans to pay off, and look up a current number with the Treasurer or the county property search before you sign anything.

The deed carries its own cost. Under 68 O.S. Section 3201, Oklahoma applies a documentary stamp tax of 75 cents on each $500 of consideration. Deeds are recorded by the County Clerk, whose website has an e-recording portal and a land records search.

  1. Look up your parcel on the county property search.
  2. Phone the Treasurer for what is owed today.
  3. Mention any exemption you hold when you talk with the title company.
  4. Make sure the deed is headed to the County Clerk for recording.

Behind on taxes and also staring at repairs or a hail-damaged roof? An as-is offer lets the payoff be handled at closing. See our Oklahoma capital gains guide for the income tax side of the same sale.

In a county this populous, a listing has plenty of competition. A financed buyer brings an appraiser and an inspector, and either can turn up repair demands. Shingles, gutters, windows and a storm shelter are the usual targets. Needing work leaves you two paths: pay for repairs before listing, or hand the house over as it stands.

As-is tends to fit when taxes are behind, an estate needs closing out, you already moved away, or cash for repairs is simply not there. A direct buyer reviews condition, names a price and takes care of the payoff at closing. Request that number in writing before committing.

Before you call anyone, gather a few items: your parcel number, a recent tax statement, any valuation notice, the deed information and any hail or storm claim paperwork. Having these on the table makes a quote faster and cuts down on back-and-forth with the title company.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of a home in Oklahoma County?
faqs.a: The County Assessor, in Suite 313 at 320 Robert S. Kerr Avenue in Oklahoma City. Increase notices tend to arrive February through April.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest a higher valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty days, counted from the notice's mailing date, to file in writing. If the decision disappoints you, the County Board of Equalization is the next stop, within 15 calendar days.

faqs.q: When are Oklahoma County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The whole bill or the first half by December 31, then the second half by March 31. A bill left unpaid is delinquent on January 1 and picks up 1.5 percent monthly interest on the 15th.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It removes $1,000 of assessed value, worth about $87 to $134 depending on location in the county. The application window runs January 1 to March 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house with back taxes owing?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from your proceeds at closing. The title company arranges the payoff, so get an up-to-date amount before signing.
